findings.title: id=27 errorHandlingChallenge - unauthenticated raw error responses are neither gracefully nor consistently handled (Accept-header representation differential)
findings.analysis: Unauthenticated GET /rest/user/security-question returns a raw 500 error containing internal stack-trace detail and an unmasked Sequelize WHERE clause, both of which are internal implementation artifacts. The exposure is inconsistent: on the identical route, changing only the Accept header from text/html to application/json changes the 500 body shape (raw HTML error with WHERE clause vs JSON error object), proving the handler does not consistently normalize or gracefully wrap errors. A second, independent GET /redirect?continue= trigger returns a raw TypeError with full stack. Benign unauthenticated routes (/api/Nonexistent/1, /rest/admin) return graceful 500 'Unexpected path' wrappers without stack traces, confirming the trigger routes are not following the application's normal graceful-wrapping path. This directly matches the challenge description 'errors are neither very gracefully nor consistently handled'. Verification (2026-10-05T21:18-21:19Z, this boot): GET /rest/user/security-question with Accept:text/html -> 500/2954 B, sha256 0bdb5e99afd039def599c67e69770b859cc5edde846279f8ca3e567a1239b2bb (byte-stable x2 in-session); same request with Accept:application/json -> 500/1812 B different body shape, sha256 402c61179cf6d4020d36da68ac16f9b1a0b98c335bf287a14f59f3210af06990; independent trigger GET /redirect?continue=http://example.com -> 500/2539 B TypeError + full stack, sha256 4ba9175e074beb81fc060f60b6c21d56e89aa1d1abeb5f3577590bd02d18ce7e (byte-stable x2 in-session); null controls GET /api/Nonexistent/1 -> 500/2444 B graceful 'Unexpected path' (no stack), GET /rest/admin -> 500/2430 B graceful (no stack). Known mutation-fragility: the /rest/user/password-hash stack-trace trigger route was wrapped to 'Unexpected path' on this boot and prior boots; the security-question and redirect triggers remain the stable class on this variant.
findings.false_positive_check: Not a benign framework default: the application's normal path for unknown/broken routes is a graceful 500 'Unexpected path' wrapper without stack detail (verified on /api/Nonexistent/1 and /rest/admin). The two trigger routes instead expose internal stack traces and raw database WHERE syntax, a materially different (non-graceful, inconsistent) behavior. Not a credential/auth issue: no credentials, secrets, or user data are in the response bodies; the impact is information disclosure of internal implementation detail via non-graceful/unconsistent error handling. Differential control (Accept header) and null controls run on the same boot and both pass. Cross-boot raw-byte drift is documented (drift_notice) and does not affect the classification.

findings.title: id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge - unauthenticated Prometheus-format /metrics endpoint serves application usage telemetry (juiceshop_llm_* gauges and challenge counters)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics on the unauthenticated application returns a 200 Prometheus-format text/plain response containing internal usage telemetry, including juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total/output_tokens_total and juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total gauges (an LLM integration's token usage), plus http_requests_count, file_uploads_count, process_* and nodejs_* runtime metrics, juiceshop_version_info, and juiceshop_challenges_solved challenge-completion counters. The endpoint requires no authentication or authorization (an invalid Bearer token returns the same 200 with the same telemetry), so any unauthenticated actor can enumerate application usage, LLM activity, startup duration, request volume, and per-difficulty/category challenge progress. This matches the 'exposedMetricsChallenge' description. Verification (2026-10-05T21:18-21:19Z, this boot): GET /metrics -> 200/26176 B text/plain, sha256 4d71a8790161407746ca84ef8afb27b42d7a6c6c672bd1c26e8bc0b7a6e5445d; invalid-Bearer GET /metrics -> 200 (no auth gate); body contains juiceshop_llm_* gauges and http_requests_count; response body is secrets-clean (no private keys, API tokens, passwords, or credentials observed in the 26 kB telemetry).
findings.false_positive_check: Not a benign or auth-gated telemetry route: an explicit invalid Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer invalid-token) does not change the response (still 200 with the same telemetry), proving the route is not protected by bearer authentication. The metrics are internal observability data (LLM token usage, request counts, challenge-solved counters, Node.js runtime state) not intended for public exposure; this is an information-disclosure / misconfiguration finding, not data breach - the response contains no secrets or user data (verified via full-body scan). Not a standard HealthCheck or public version endpoint: the response is Prometheus exposition format with Juice Shop-specific metrics prefixes, distinct from the SPA home page (200/9393 B) or API envelope. Body byte-drift across reads is documented (drift_notice, counters increment between reads) and does not affect classification.
